blocks.h2: What Happens After a Burst Pipe Is Fixed
blocks.body: Once the pipe is repaired and the water is back on, the drying starts. Wet drywall, insulation and flooring need to dry fully, or mold can follow. A restoration company can measure moisture and dry the space properly. We'll show you where the pipe froze and why, and suggest simple changes, like insulation, a heat source or rerouting, so the same spot doesn't freeze next winter.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: Do you offer frozen pipe services?
items.answer: Yes. We thaw frozen lines safely and repair any that split.

items.q: Can I thaw a frozen pipe myself?
items.answer: Open the faucet and warm the pipe gently with a hair dryer. Never use a flame. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: How do I keep pipes from freezing?
items.preview: Heat, open cabinets and a slow drip.
items.answer: Keep the heat on, open cabinets on exterior walls and let a faucet drip on the coldest nights.
Often. Policies vary, so check with your agent.

items.q: Which pipes freeze most in Elmhurst homes?
items.preview: Those on outside walls and in garages.
items.answer: Pipes on outside walls, in attached garages and in crawl spaces under additions.

items.q: Should I shut off the water before a trip in winter?
items.answer: It's a good idea for longer trips, as long as the heat stays on.
